question: Given a Seurat object RDS file, automate cell type annotation for each cluster using SingleR and save a UMAP plot with cells colored by cell type annotation.

files.eval_guideline: Cells colored by cell type label on a UMAP layout; axis labels and color scheme may differ.
files.match_reasoning: The filenames match exactly and both files are PNG images of the SingleR UMAP plot.
files.strategy_reasoning: The output is a PNG plot, and the guideline asks for a visual check: a UMAP layout with cells colored by SingleR cell type labels, where axis labels and colors may differ. A semantic comparison is the right way to judge that kind of plot content.

comparison_details.explanation:
Both images show the same PBMC UMAP embedding. The coordinates are identical: a monocyte branch at upper left (x about -10 to -5, y about 2 to 6), a platelet cluster near (-5.5, 9), a large T/NK island at the right (x about 0 to 7.5), and a B-cell island near (2, -14). Both colour the cells by SingleR cell-type labels and place text labels on the plot. The major annotations agree: Monocyte, T_cells, NK_cell, B_cell and Platelets are in the same locations in both images.

Differences:
(1) The reference appears to use per-cell SingleR labels. It therefore includes minor scattered labels (Pre-B_cell_CD34-, CMP and Pro-B_cell_CD34+) sprinkled within the main clusters. The candidate uses cluster-level annotation, as the task wording requires ("for each cluster"), so it has only 5 labels and no minor ones.
(2) The NK/T boundary differs. In the reference, NK cells are mainly at the far-right tip (x about 6 to 7.5), with T cells reaching about x = 6. In the candidate, the NK label covers a larger part of the T/NK island (x about 3 to 7.5), probably because a whole cluster was labelled NK.
(3) Presentation differs: the colour palette, the candidate's added title ("HPCA reference"), the axis label text and the aspect ratio. None of these matter here.

The overall scientific message is the same: the layout is identical, the major cell types agree, and both are valid SingleR annotations. The differences come from per-cell versus cluster-level labelling, which slightly changes the NK/T split and removes the rare minor labels.

files.eval_guideline: Per-cell label assignments must match the reference; row order and label capitalisation may differ.
files.match_reasoning: The filenames match exactly and both files are CSV tables of SingleR annotations.

parameters.question: Compare per-cell SingleR cell type annotations from a Seurat PBMC object; per-cell label assignments must match the reference, row order and label capitalisation may differ.

files.strategy_reasoning: The guideline requires each cell's label to match the reference, but row order and capitalisation can differ. SingleR is deterministic, so approximate (record-level alignment that ignores row order and case) is the right fit.

align_plan.reasoning: The tables have the same orientation, one row per cell (2638 each), so no transpose is needed. Rows are matched on 'barcodes', the unique cell barcode in both tables. The order of rows doesn't matter: the guideline says per-cell assignments are compared and row order may differ. The reference 'labels' column holds per-cell SingleR labels. In all 10 preview rows it matches the candidate's 'cell_level_labels', including rows 6-8, where the reference and 'cell_level_labels' both say T_cells. The candidate's own 'labels' column is a per-cluster label (NK_cell for cluster 2) and differs from the reference in those rows. Because the guideline asks for per-cell labels, 'labels' is mapped to 'cell_level_labels'. 'cell_level_pruned_labels' was not chosen because it may contain NA values from pruning. The extra columns (cluster, UMAP_1, UMAP_2) are left out. Capitalisation differences in labels are allowed by the guideline.

column_configs.name: labels
column_configs.reasoning: Each cell's label must match the reference. Cell-type names carry meaning, so an exact match is the right test, not partition relabelling. Labels are single values, so no delimiter or overlap scoring is needed. Labels should be case-normalised first, because the guideline allows capitalisation differences.

comparison_plan.overall_reasoning: The only data column to compare is 'labels', the SingleR cell-type label for each cell. Rows are aligned on barcodes, which is excluded from the comparison. The guideline says each cell's label must match the reference, so I chose an exact cell-by-cell match on the label column. Cell types are named biological categories, not arbitrary group IDs, so 'partition' (which relabels groups to find the best fit) does not apply. The guideline allows capitalisation to differ, so the labels should be case-normalised before matching. The candidate also has extra columns (cluster, cell_level_pruned_labels, UMAP_1, UMAP_2) that are not in the reference, so they are not compared. Note that the candidate's cluster-level labels (labels__candidate) differ from the reference's per-cell labels in some rows, for example cluster 2 cells that the reference calls T_cells. The exact match will correctly count these as mismatches.
